rationale: C21 plausibly supplied a concrete medal-order template: both establish a named military medal with suitable appurtenances, authorize awards under regulations severally prescribed by service secretaries, identify eligible service members, and define eligibility through service during specified periods. C13 reinforces the same medal-eligibility drafting pattern but lacks C21's especially close establishment-and-regulation language. C24 uses related medal-award machinery but is more elaborate and less textually aligned.

shared_material.child_excerpt: There is hereby established the Good Conduct Medal, which shall include suitable appurtenances.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: There is hereby established the Korean Service Medal, with suitable appurtenances
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive near-verbatim establishment language for a named medal and its appurtenances.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Such medal may be awarded ... under such regulations as the Secretary of the Army and the Secretary of the Air Force shall severally prescribe
shared_material.parent_excerpt: for award, under such regulations as the Secretaries of the Army, Navy, and Air Force and the Secretary of the Treasury may severally prescribe
shared_material.explanation: The same administrative mechanism delegates medal-award rules severally to the relevant service secretaries.

shared_material.child_excerpt: to those enlisted men ... who on or after August 27, 1940 ... or who after December 7, 1941 ... or who ... have completed a period of honorable service
shared_material.parent_excerpt: to members of the armed forces of the United States who during any period between June 27, 1950 ... and a terminal date ... shall have served
shared_material.explanation: Both follow the establishment and delegation clauses with service-based eligibility tied to expressly defined temporal periods.
